fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled JPEG bytes are parsed to obtain width, height, and subsampling; the return value is ignored, so malformed/truncated images proceed.
First transform requests progressive output with COPYNONE, so the destination buffer is sized from source dimensions and markers are not copied.
Destination buffer is allocated using tjBufSize(width, height, jpegSubsamp); for 4:2:2/4:4:0/4:1:1 subsampling this size is not commutative with swapped width/height.
The source JPEG is fully decoded into coefficient arrays; if the scan data is truncated or malformed, some coefficient blocks remain at their pre-zeroed state while others are filled.
Destination compressor parameters (including subsampling and dimensions) are copied from the source decompressor.
The destination compressor is initialized with the transformed coefficient arrays; compress_output will later read these blocks during encoding.
The transform operation (JXFORM_NONE with no crop) is executed; for JXFORM_NONE with no crop, no workspace is needed and dstcoefs aliases srccoefs.
Pointers to DCT blocks from the coefficient arrays are assembled into MCU_buffer; blocks that were never filled by the truncated decoder retain pre-zeroed values.
The sequential Huffman encoder is invoked on each DCT block; the block contents are read as coefficients.

The DC coefficient is read from the block; if the block was never initialized by the decoder (truncated scan data), this reads uninitialized memory, triggering the MSAN Use-of-uninitialized-value report.
